title: Future: I will write, I'm going to write

blocks.text: The imperfective verb has 3 tenses: the present, the past, and the future. The perfective verb has 2 tenses: the past and the future.
**Future tense after «когда» and «как только».** In a sentence referring to the future with a subordinate clause introduced by "when" or "as soon as" the verbs of both clauses are in the future:

items: Я буду читать письма, когда ты будешь учить диалог.

blocks.text: An action of the subordinate clause which is to be completed before the action of the main clause is rendered by the perfective future:

items: Когда я сделаю уроки, я буду слушать радио.
Как только я получу от него письмо, я напишу вам.

blocks.text: The future condition is expressed in English by the present tense, whereas in Russian it is expressed by the future: *Я пойду в школу завтра, если я буду здоров.* — I'll go to school tomorrow if I am well.

items: We will ask at a travel agency.
I will not see him any more.
Now you will start to warm up.
No one will notice the substitution.
